clue.text: Sweetheart cycling and old man reeling come together

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the front letter of the word rides round to the back

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart

indicators.note: reeling means spinning backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A romantic scene: a sweetheart out on a bike and a staggering old father meet up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' and 'reeling' look like the couple's movements, but both are instructions: one sends a letter round from front to back, the other turns a word round. Old man is a familiar British term for one's father.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things overlap when they extend over each other and partly coincide, so they meet or coincide in part.

clue.text: Unconscious, ducks squashed by drive in the park?

parts.note: a boxer knocked out cold is out, unconscious

indicators.note: the ducks are squeezed between the letters of the road, so they go inside

parts.note: DR is the street-name abbreviation for drive
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O, so two ducks give OO

explanation.surface: A sad picture of senseless ducks flattened by traffic on a drive through a park.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket, written as the letter O. 'squashed by' puts the ducks inside the abbreviation for drive, giving DOOR. The question mark: a park is just one place that is open-air.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything in a park is in the open air, which is what outdoor means; the question mark admits the definition is by example.

clue.text: Heart possibly found in grave

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: the word earth, shattered, could be rearranged to give heart

explanation.surface: A morbid hint that a heart might turn up buried in a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: the clue's opening words are the result of the answer's instructions. Take EARTH and shatter it and you could get HEART. 'found in' only links this to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentous enough to shake the world is weighty and serious in its consequences, a sense of grave.

clue.text: Partly finances a crew Olympians set up with no capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so the letters are read in reverse
partly means only a part of the words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the letters run through the end of the first word, the next two words and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A sporting news item: money pays for a rowing crew of Olympic athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' picks out ESACREWOL from the end of finances to the start of Olympians, and 'set up' reverses it, reading up the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters, as opposed to capitals, are called this after the printer's lower type case where they were kept.

clue.text: Collar and cuff should get one to replace uniform

indicators.note: the word should get a new letter, a hint that one of its letters will be swapped for another
the numeral one takes the place of the letter for uniform

parts.note: a cuff is a blow with the hand, a punch
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Tailoring advice: a collar and a cuff need one new item in place of the uniform's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar and cuff' looks like shirt parts, but 'Collar' is the definition and 'cuff' means a blow. 'should get one to replace uniform' swaps the U of PUNCH for I.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, to collar and to pinch both mean to arrest someone, as a police officer does.

clue.text: Confusion from yours truly — darling left to go west

parts.note: yours truly is a jocular way of saying me

indicators.note: in an across clue west is the start, so the L for left moves from the back to the front

parts.note: angel is a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.surface: Someone owning up to a mix-up: their darling has gone to the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left to go west' means the letter L (left) heads west, to the front of ANGEL, giving LANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a jumbled mixture of things, so a confused medley.

clue.text: Guru RFK Jr's message goes over head of ex-PM

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece goes over, above, the other

parts.note: Robert F Kennedy Jr's slogan is Make America Healthy Again, abbreviated MAHA
Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister 2022 to 2024; his first name heads his full name

explanation.surface: A political mash-up: the American health campaigner's slogan sails over a former British prime minister's head.
explanation.walkthrough: MAHA is Robert F Kennedy Jr's health campaign; in this down clue 'goes over' puts it on top. 'head of ex-PM' is the first name of Rishi Sunak, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu sage or spiritual teacher, so a guru.

clue.text: Had a smoke — pitiful, but not if smashed

indicators.note: smashed means broken to pieces, so the letters reassemble in a new order
the word that follows is excluded from the letters

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A smoker's excuse: lighting up was pathetic, but not if you were drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' looks like drunk in the surface, but it shuffles PITUL, what 'but not' leaves of pitiful once IF is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To light up is to ignite a cigarette or pipe, so having lit up is having had a smoke.

clue.text: Organ on pier where Ed airs his compositions?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: an organ is a publication that voices views, such as a newspaper
a pier is a supporting pillar, a column

explanation.surface: A seaside picture: an organ playing on a pier where someone called Ed performs his music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'pier' suggest a seaside bandstand, but an organ is a publication and a pier is a supporting pillar; 'on' stacks one above the other in this down clue. Ed is an editor, whose compositions are written pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor's opinion pieces appear in a regular slot in the paper, the place he airs his writings.

clue.text: Volunteers went without clothes on more than one programme

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
stripped of its covering, the outer letters of the word come off

parts.note: its middle letters are used
a list is a programme of items, so lists are programmes

explanation.surface: A naturist story: people went naked on several television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without clothes' strips W and T from went, leaving EN, which sits 'on' top of the programmes in this down clue. 'Volunteers' is a verb here, signs up, not a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enlists signs up voluntarily for the armed forces, so volunteers for service.

clue.text: Two pieces of fabric fencing in the step down

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the two words wrap round the words that follow

parts.note: a throw is a cloth draped over furniture, and a towel is a cloth for drying
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sewing or upholstery: two lengths of material are used to fence in a step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like sport or a garden boundary, but here it means surrounding. The phrase comes from boxing, where a corner throws in the towel to concede the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit defeat and quit is to throw in the towel, so to resign or step down from a post.

clue.text: River dweller becoming hard-hearted and separate

indicators.note: the middle letter turns into a different one, the old letter becoming the new
points to the heart, the middle letter of the animal's name

parts.note: an otter lives in rivers
the heart of the animal's name, its middle letter
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An animal story: a riverbank creature turns callous and goes its own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard-hearted' reads as cruel, but splits into 'hard', H, and 'hearted', its middle letter: 'becoming' swaps the central T of OTTER for H.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means different or distinct from the one already mentioned, as separate does.

clue.text: Wishes to entertain seamen with special number for dances

indicators.note: to entertain is to take someone in as a guest, so these letters go inside

parts.note: hopes are wishes
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for the seamen of the British fleet
pi is the mathematical constant, a number with special status

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to entertain sailors with a special song and dance number.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy, crossword shorthand for sailors. 'to entertain' puts RN and PI inside HOPES, after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors, so these are dances.

clue.text: Judges, penned by prophet, on reflection keeps repeating

indicators.note: penned in by the reversed prophet, the judging verb goes inside
reflected as in a mirror, the word is read backwards

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
a judge hears a case, so hears means judges

explanation.surface: A biblical scene: the judges of Israel are held captive by a prophet who, on reflection, keeps saying the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' is the verb, as a judge hears a case, not the Old Testament book that the nearby prophet suggests. 'on reflection' and 'penned by' work on the prophet and judges in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise by going over something again and again, so to keep repeating it.

clue.text: With Barbie's boy engaged, proof's going about she's this

indicators.note: engaged means held inside, so the doll's name goes inside the other letters
going about suggests the letters move around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written without its apostrophe, as anagram material
Ken is the boyfriend doll of Barbie

explanation.surface: Gossip: with Barbie's boyfriend engaged, evidence is circulating of who she's tied to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' rearranges the letters of proof's (the apostrophe is ignored) to SPOFOR, and 'engaged' holds the doll inside. Read whole, Barbie herself is the 'she' who is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone already engaged to be married is taken, reserved for another, so she is no longer available.

clue.text: For example Samuel squeaks when talking

indicators.note: when talking means as spoken, so the word is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: peeps are high squeaking sounds, as from chicks

explanation.surface: A nursery scene: a child named Samuel squeaks whenever he speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: Samuel Pepys, the 17th-century diarist, is one person with the surname, which 'when talking' sounds the same as the squeaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys, the English naval administrator famed for his diary, is one bearer of the surname.

clue.text: Catastrophe! No men allowed to box in spectacles

indicators.note: the answer is boxed in by the surrounding words, enclosed within them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the middle words to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A notice at a boxing club: disaster, as men may no longer box wearing glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to box in' and 'spectacles' suggest boxing in glasses, but 'to box in' signals the answer is enclosed in the clue's opening words. The exclamation mark is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable sights or events, so spectacles; the plural matches.

clue.text: Right time to cut through part of roof?

indicators.note: the letter cuts through the roofing word, ending up inside it

parts.note: a tile is one piece of a roof covering

explanation.surface: A builder asks if this is the right moment to cut into a section of roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an adjective agreeing with 'time', but it is the noun meaning a legal claim. 'to cut through' puts T inside TILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Title is a legal right to ownership of property, as in holding title to land.

clue.text: Out-of-town visitor, type who goes on and on about double parking

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so this word goes round the other piece

parts.words: type who goes on and on
parts.note: a trier keeps on trying, persevering
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking, so double parking is two of them

explanation.surface: A complaint about an outsider who drones endlessly about people parking two abreast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double parking' looks like a traffic offence, but it means two of the P road-sign abbreviation. 'type who goes on and on' is someone who perseveres, not a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a tripper is someone on a day trip or short excursion, a tourist from out of town.

clue.text: One produces oil to relieve shakes

indicators.note: shakes means jumbles, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Advice about oil as a remedy to relieve the shakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One produces oil' could be a refinery or a well; it is a tree. 'shakes' rearranges TO RELIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive tree bears the fruit that is pressed for olive oil, so it produces oil.

clue.text: Spirit seen in German city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr region of Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A ghostly presence spotted in a church in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a ghost in the church, but it means the inner nature of something. CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its intrinsic nature or core quality, its spirit.

clue.text: Cool coverage pitched Soho event as oddly overlooked

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are passed over, leaving the even ones

parts.note: taken as written; its second, fourth, sixth letters and so on are used

explanation.surface: A trendy party in London's Soho district was pitched as something unusual and then ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly overlooked' skips letters 1, 3, 5 and so on, leaving every second letter of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice sheets are vast layers of glacier ice covering land, a frozen blanket, so a cold covering.

clue.text: Popular overhead railway in Philly, maybe board here?

parts.note: hot means in demand, popular
the El is the American name for an elevated railway, as in Philadelphia or Chicago

explanation.surface: A tourist asks if this is where to get on Philadelphia's popular elevated train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like getting on a train, but it is board as in bed and board: food and lodging. Philly is Philadelphia.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel provides board, meals and accommodation, so it is a place to lodge.

clue.text: This could be beach volleyball wear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a game or athletic activity, of which beach volleyball is an example
second meaning: to ... something is to wear it proudly, as in ... a beard

explanation.walkthrough: 'beach volleyball wear' reads as swimsuits, but it splits: beach volleyball is an example of the first sense, and 'wear' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a competitive game and a verb for showing off something on your person.

clue.text: Orchestra Musicians love the sound of violin players!

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than spelt, rhyming with toes

parts.note: bows are what play a violin's strings

explanation.surface: Musicians in an orchestra love listening to the violins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violin players' is not the violinists but their bows, and 'the sound of' turns BOWS into the like-sounding BOES. Love is O, as in a tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: The double-reed woodwind instruments are part of the orchestra, and the name also stands for their players.

clue.text: Crunch time for Wimbledon ace?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the decisive moment after which there is no going back
second meaning: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch, a winner that is never sent back

explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship. An ace is a serve the opponent never touches, so it is literally a point that is not returned.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the critical stage after which reversal is impossible, and literally describes an unreturned serve.

clue.text: German pistol used as revolver, a resistance standard

indicators.note: a revolver turns round, so the pistol's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A weapons note: a German pistol pressed into service as a revolver as standard by the Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used as revolver' makes the pistol revolve, read backwards as REGUL, rather than describing its mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means normal or usual, conforming to the standard size or type.

clue.text: Rookie golfer's start interrupted by bad weather

indicators.note: the weather breaks into the golf word, going inside it

parts.note: a golfer starts each hole from the tee
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: A novice golfer's first round is halted by a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golfer's start' is the tee each hole starts from; 'interrupted by' puts RAIN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone still learning a job, a newcomer or novice like a rookie.
